bundle: Sonniss #GameAudioGDC Bundle 2024, the nine folders Sonniss.com-GDC2024-GameAudioBundle1of9 to 9of9
licence: The Sonniss #GameAudioGDC Bundle Licensing Agreement, the file 'License - GDC Game Audio.pdf' of the bundle (it prints no version number)

sounds.listenFirst: A blade drawn along metal stands in for the swing; the other is a designed energy sword.
sounds.why: The Melee Weapons library has no swing or whoosh, only scrapes, drops and hits. A slow sword scrape is the nearest thing to a blade in motion; the anime library's sword cut is the only designed sword sound of the bundle.

candidates.take: The eighth of ten scrapes (16.89 to 17.54 s), the one with the quickest rise.
candidates.note: A metal scrape that swells for 150 ms and rings out, around 5 kHz; 0.45 s.

candidates.take: The cut itself (it starts at 0.08 s), without the low tail that follows to 1.05 s.
candidates.note: A sharp attack and a tone that climbs from 1.5 to 2.4 kHz in 150 ms: a designed 'shing', more science fiction; 0.39 s.

sounds.listenFirst: The kept laser has a low body; the alternative is a noisier zap.
sounds.why: The Martian ray wants a cartoon laser. The anime laser beam is named for it; the science-fiction 'zap' is the only other short energy sound whose energy is not all below 150 Hz.

candidates.take: The first of three identical takes; its opening burst, without the two-second low tail.
candidates.note: A burst at 0.8 to 1.5 kHz for 200 ms, then a low body around 300 Hz; 0.5 s.

candidates.take: The first half second of a 1.9 s zap, faded out.
candidates.note: A broad noisy crackle centred near 1.1 kHz, no clear pitch, steadier and rougher than the laser; 0.5 s.

sounds.why: Nothing in the bundle is named a spell or a bolt. A plasma fly-by is offered for comparison; the generated dark bolt stays the default.

candidates.take: The loud middle of a 2 s fly-by: its rise and pass, without the low tail.
candidates.note: A broad whoosh that swells over 300 ms, centred at 1 to 1.7 kHz, then sinks; 0.9 s, three times the length of the generated bolt.

sounds.why: A flare leaving its tube for the Rocket Cart's firework.

candidates.take: The flare shot (the first event, 0 to 0.64 s), without the burst that follows at 0.84 s.
candidates.note: A noisy launch at 1 to 3 kHz for a quarter of a second; 0.5 s.

sounds.listenFirst: It is one shot, where the generated sound is a burst.
sounds.why: A steampunk gun for the Clockwork Gunner. The firearm libraries of parts 3 to 6 are real pistols, rifles and automatic fire and were left out.

candidates.take: The shot itself (it starts at 0.19 s), without the mechanism clicks before it and the long tail.
candidates.note: A single dry shot with a short tail; 0.44 s.

sounds.why: Name and unit match: a steampunk cannon for the Steam Cannon.

candidates.take: The shot and the first 0.8 s of its 3.8 s tail.
candidates.note: A cannon shot with its body; 0.8 s.

sounds.why: The Kawaii UI library has a cartoon pop by name; a cork leaving a glass bottle is the natural alternative.

candidates.take: The pop (0.03 to 0.06 s) and its short ring.
candidates.note: One dry pop of 20 ms around 0.8 kHz with a faint low ring; 0.14 s.

candidates.take: The second of six events: a cork pulled, with the bottle's ring.
candidates.note: A brighter pop (energy to 8 kHz) followed by the bottle ringing at 1.1 kHz; 0.15 s.

sounds.listenFirst: The most played sound of a match.
sounds.why: A cartoon punch. Both anime libraries have one; a cardboard box thump is a softer, duller option.

candidates.take: The first of four punches in a row (they come 0.3 s apart): a thump at 0.12 s and its burst of noise.
candidates.note: A thump and 80 ms of noise around 2 kHz; 0.26 s.

candidates.take: The last of the four hits (0.62 s), the only one with room to ring out.
candidates.note: A harder smack with more low end (half its energy below 150 Hz) and a rattling tail; 0.3 s.

candidates.take: The first of two thumps.
candidates.note: A soft, dull thud around 100 to 300 Hz, nothing above 1 kHz; 0.26 s.

sounds.why: A tight heavy thud. The kept steampunk impact has the most weight; a hammered oil barrel and a dropped plastic pipe are hollower.

candidates.take: The impact (0.05 to 0.25 s and its ring), without the click that comes 50 ms before it.
candidates.note: A thud near 100 Hz with a knock at 1.9 kHz; 0.41 s.

candidates.library: Pole Position - The Metal Hit Sweeteners Library
candidates.take: The third of ten hammer blows.
candidates.note: A hollow metal bonk at 200 to 1000 Hz, shorter and lighter; 0.22 s.

candidates.library: Pole Position - The Plastic Textures Library
candidates.originalFile: Flexible Sewer Pipe Big - Broken - DROP - Thump - Mono.wav
candidates.take: The sixth of nine drops, the one that starts with the thump.
candidates.note: A low thump near 80 Hz with a plastic rattle after it; 0.27 s.

sounds.why: A medium explosion; the other explosions of the bundle are nuclear, a car, a rocket through a car roof and a distant mine.

candidates.take: The blast and the first second of its tail (the file is one explosion of 1.9 s).
candidates.note: A full explosion with its rumble; 1.05 s.

sounds.listenFirst: Glass stands in for ice in all three.
sounds.why: Nothing in the bundle is breaking ice, so glass stands in. Three kinds: falling shards, one break, a small clink.

candidates.take: The first half second: the break and the shards up to the second burst at 0.44 s.
candidates.note: Glass shards falling, 3 to 9 kHz; 0.52 s.

candidates.take: The break and its falling pieces (0.08 to 0.6 s).
candidates.note: One hard break, brighter (centre near 9 kHz) with three bursts of pieces after it; 0.55 s.

candidates.library: Sonic Bat - Videogame Foley Essentials Vol. II
candidates.take: The whole clink, a quiet recording brought up to level.
candidates.note: A small light clink and a second touch 150 ms later, 6 to 11 kHz; 0.3 s.

sounds.listenFirst: Both come from a library sold for gore; they are wet food foley, but hear them before anyone else does.
sounds.why: A wet splat for the pie and the acid. The only splats of the bundle are in the Gore Mini Pack (made with fruit and vegetables); the designed water impacts of part 1 are nearly all below 150 Hz.

candidates.take: The third of six splatters, the shortest.
candidates.note: A wet burst at 2 to 5 kHz that lands in 30 ms and spatters for 0.4 s; 0.46 s.

candidates.take: The fifth drop: the slap and the wet patter after it.
candidates.note: A heavier slap with a low thud under it, then a thin wet patter at 6 to 8 kHz; 0.43 s.

sounds.why: The Melee Weapons library has shield blocks by name. Most of a block's energy is a low thud, so its bright first 50 ms carry it; a ringing metal impact is the clangier alternative.

candidates.take: The first of five blocks.
candidates.note: A bright metallic crack, then a body thud that fades in 0.3 s; little ring; 0.42 s.

candidates.take: The impact and its ring (0.07 to 0.6 s).
candidates.note: A clang that rings at 1.3 kHz for half a second: more bell than block; 0.58 s.

sounds.listenFirst: Neither is a plain splash: one is water stirred, the other a plop heard under water.
sounds.why: Water moving. The bundle's water is streams, drips, drains and hydrophone recordings; a hand moving through water is the closest to a splash.

candidates.take: The loud part of the second of eight movements.
candidates.note: A soft slosh at 0.7 to 1.6 kHz that swells and falls away; 0.95 s.

candidates.take: The impact (0.15 s) and the first bubbles after it.
candidates.note: A round plop at 380 Hz and quiet bubbling: recorded under water, so it has no spray; 0.65 s.

sounds.why: The bundle has no cartoon voice. A man's sharp gasp and a pig's squeal are offered for comparison; the generated sound stays the default.

candidates.originalFile: HMNBrth_Human, Adult, Male, Breath, Surprise, Gasp_UberDuo_INHL_17.wav
candidates.take: The gasp itself.
candidates.note: A breathy indrawn gasp, a real human voice; 0.27 s.

candidates.take: The squeal, without the snort that follows.
candidates.note: A pig's squeal that falls from 1.3 kHz to 0.7 kHz: comic, and unmistakably a pig; 0.63 s.

sounds.why: No cartoon death in the bundle. An anime 'charge down' (a falling whistle) is offered for comparison; the generated sound stays the default.

candidates.take: The first 0.8 s of a 1.3 s fall, faded out.
candidates.note: A clean tone gliding down from 2 kHz to 0.5 kHz, bright (its overtones sit near 5 kHz); 0.77 s.

sounds.listenFirst: A chess piece on a board, not a footstep.
sounds.why: The bundle has no footstep on grass or earth (only heavy mechanical ones, a horse's trot and skis). A chess piece set down on its board suits a unit moved on a board.

candidates.take: The third of three contacts.
candidates.note: A wooden tock at 0.5 to 1.4 kHz with a low thump under it; 0.14 s.

candidates.take: The second contact.
candidates.note: A lighter, shorter tock around 350 Hz without the thump; 0.09 s.

sounds.listenFirst: It climbs to 5.9 kHz and may be piercing.
sounds.why: An anime power-up for a promotion.

candidates.take: The third of four takes (6.15 to 6.83 s), the shortest: a tone that climbs from 0.75 to 5.9 kHz in half a second.
candidates.note: A tone sweeping up from 0.75 to 5.9 kHz in half a second; 0.74 s.

sounds.why: No war horn or drum. A cinematic low brass blast is offered for comparison; the generated call stays the default.

candidates.take: The first 1.35 s of a 6.5 s blast, faded out.
candidates.note: A low brass swell on one note (75 Hz with its overtones near 350 Hz): heavy and dark for this game; 1.35 s.

sounds.why: A glass 'dark tone' is offered for comparison; the growls and sinister textures of part 1 are horror. The generated sound stays the default.

candidates.take: The first second of a 2.6 s tone.
candidates.note: A hollow pulsing tone at 280 and 570 Hz that swells and dies away; eerie rather than comic; 1.05 s.

sounds.why: A reversed metal ring (a sound that is sucked in) is offered for comparison. The generated sound stays the default.

candidates.take: The last 1.2 s of the reversed ring: the swell up to its sudden end.
candidates.note: A tone at 300 Hz that grows louder and brighter for a second and stops dead; 1.24 s.

sounds.why: Three short science-fiction transitions are offered for comparison (bead 2yc.20 found them too generic to choose one). The generated beam stays the default.

candidates.take: The whole transition.
candidates.note: A bright shimmer that falls from 9 kHz to 3 kHz and ends on a tone near 2.2 kHz: a beam coming down; 1 s.

candidates.take: The whole transition.
candidates.note: A noisy swell and fade centred at 3 to 5 kHz, no pitch; 0.95 s.

candidates.take: The whole zoom; it ends abruptly by design.
candidates.note: A buzzing tone on 190 Hz that grows for half a second and cuts off: a zoom in; 0.6 s.

sounds.why: Ice by name: ice sizzling as it cracks in water. A reversed glass swell is the designed alternative.

candidates.take: The onset of an 8.5 s sizzle and its first 0.7 s.
candidates.note: A crisp crackle at 5 to 7 kHz that starts hard and thins out; 0.79 s.

candidates.take: The swell of the reversed break up to its stop.
candidates.note: A glassy hiss near 10 kHz that rises in three steps and stops dead; 0.55 s.

sounds.why: Falling rock and earth for a tunnelling Mole.

candidates.take: 0.85 s from the start of a 5.3 s rumble of falling rock, with its own fades.
candidates.note: A rumble of falling rock with its own fades; 0.85 s.

sounds.why: A shell cracking: snapped celery (from the gore pack's 'bone breaks', which are a vegetable) and a snapped twig. A chick's cheeps are the comic alternative.

candidates.take: Three crackles from the end of the fourth break.
candidates.note: Three dry crackles 150 to 250 ms apart, 3 to 6 kHz; 0.5 s.

candidates.take: The two snaps of the fifth break.
candidates.note: Two sharper snaps 200 ms apart, brighter; 0.3 s.

candidates.take: The second of three snaps, the loud one.
candidates.note: One dry woody snap with a double crack, 3 to 4.5 kHz; 0.16 s.

candidates.take: Four cheeps from the second group.
candidates.note: A chick cheeping at 2.4 kHz: what hatches, not the shell; 0.5 s.

sounds.why: A second pop, different from the gumball's: a cork, a run of four finger pops, a tin lid.

candidates.take: The fourth of six events: the cork's pop.
candidates.note: One round pop around 500 Hz with a bright edge; 0.09 s.

candidates.take: The whole file: four pops 60 ms apart.
candidates.note: Four tiny pops climbing a chord (1.3, 1.7, 2 and 2.4 kHz): a little rising run, more of an interface sound; 0.22 s.

candidates.take: The lid coming off (0.15 to 0.27 s).
candidates.note: A hollow tonk at 500 Hz with a second knock; a quiet recording brought up to level; 0.18 s.

sounds.listenFirst: Both are hisses near 9 kHz and may be harsh.
sounds.why: Named for it: a short release of steam. The clip of bead 2yc.20 (a pneumatic hiss from an alien weapon) stays as the alternative.

candidates.take: The first half second of the third of five releases.
candidates.note: A burst of steam that holds for 0.4 s, 9 to 11 kHz; 0.53 s.

candidates.take: The first 0.38 s of a 5.7 s pneumatic hiss, faded out.
candidates.note: A shorter pneumatic hiss around 8.7 kHz that fades at once; 0.38 s.

sounds.listenFirst: Chosen from its pitch curve alone.
sounds.why: A cartoon spring for a bouncing candy unit.

candidates.take: The first of four identical takes: its first four swings (a tone going up and down between 0.4 and 1.1 kHz, each swing quieter).
candidates.note: A pure tone swinging between 0.4 and 1.1 kHz every 130 ms, each swing quieter; 0.54 s.

sounds.why: A hammer blow. Four materials: stone, iron, a staple gun and a dropped piece of wood.

candidates.take: The blow and its ring (the first 0.2 s), without the chips that fall after it.
candidates.note: A hammer on stone that rings at 5.4 kHz; 0.2 s.

candidates.take: The drop and its bounce.
candidates.note: A wooden clack at 1.7 kHz and a small bounce 150 ms later; 0.28 s.
